content.alt: 02. Brush, Brush, Sparkle Sparkle! - Is every brushing time a battle?
content.text:
Is every brushing time a battle?

The moment you say it's time to brush, your child ducks under the blanket or shakes their head no. Brushing teeth, the final gate of the day, so often turns into a nightly struggle.

There have probably been nights when you gave in to that pleading "Can't I just skip it once?" But instead of nagging or scaring them, a single story that turns brushing into a fun game can get your child to pick up the toothbrush first.

Curious about the toddler toothbrushing habit storybook plot? We take a look at the lessons of the toddler toothbrushing habit storybook alongside the illustrations. Meet the key scenes of the toddler toothbrushing habit storybook too. Read the toddler toothbrushing habit storybook together with your child and talk about the story. From a child refusing to brush teeth to a kid who won't brush teeth and toddler toothbrushing training, we've gathered all kinds of stories about 02. Brush, Brush, Sparkle Sparkle!

content.alt: 02. Brush, Brush, Sparkle Sparkle! - Why the brushing habit matters
content.text:
Why the brushing habit matters

The toddler years, when baby teeth are coming in, are the most important time to build a toothbrushing habit. When bits of food left on the teeth after meals and snacks are just left there, teeth start to feel grimy and itchy.

What's needed here isn't a scary warning, but the felt experience that brushing leaves your mouth fresh and feeling good. This small habit repeated every morning and night becomes the first button in a lifetime of healthy teeth.
content.caption: What cavity bugs fear most is toothpaste foam.

content.alt: 02. Brush, Brush, Sparkle Sparkle! - The story of Hori and the cavity bugs
content.text:
The story of Hori and the cavity bugs

Hori, the hero of Brush, Brush, Sparkle Sparkle!, finds brushing too much of a bother and falls asleep after skipping it just once. But in the middle of the night, his teeth start to itch! The cookie crumbs he ate during the day have hidden between his teeth.

In his mom's make-believe story, the toothbrush becomes a shining sword and the toothpaste foam becomes magic bubbles. Hori jumps up, dashes to the sink, and brushes up and down, chasing the cavity bugs away with frothy bubbles. When he rinses his mouth, his teeth sparkle like stars.

content.alt: 02. Brush, Brush, Sparkle Sparkle! - Putting the brushing habit into practice at home
content.text:
Putting the brushing habit into practice at home

Once you've read the story, it's time to carry it into practice at home. Here are a few ideas.

First, read this book together right before brushing. The afterglow of the story flows straight into brushing. Second, set a visible rule: once in the morning, once before bed. Third, do the up-and-down brushing motion together like a game, and when it's all done, praise loudly that the teeth are sparkling like stars.

content.text:
Frequently Asked Questions

Q. At what age should we start building a brushing habit?

A. You can lay the foundation of the habit by gently brushing from the moment the first tooth comes in. When your child wants to hold the toothbrush themselves and you start happily together, it carries on naturally.

Q. What should I do when my child hates brushing?

A. Rather than scaring them, turn it into a fun game of defeating germs with brushing. Like the hero of the toddler toothbrushing habit storybook, singing while brushing reduces the resistance.

Q. Is it okay to let them brush on their own?

A. Praise their wish to brush by themselves, but during the stage when thorough brushing is hard, it's best for a parent to help finish up together. Brushing while looking in the mirror together makes it a joyful habit.
